content.jointProblem: Can Serbian script canonicalization combined with morphological normalization reduce LinguaBot’s support-search misses while allowing vocabulary updates without a full re-index? The first experiment would compare the existing Elasticsearch pipeline with normalization-order and query-expansion variants on held-out support queries, explicitly testing within-word script mixing and new product terms; a miss rate below 5% is a hypothesis to test, not an assured outcome.

rationale.text: Dragić has directly studied the interaction between Serbian morphological reduction and script normalization, including the effect of operation order on retrieval.

sources.quote: U ovom radu ispitujemo kako stemovanje i lematizacija interaguju s postupkom normalizacije skripte pri izgradnji pretražnog indeksa.
stemovanje posle normalizacije daje konzistentno bolje rezultate za sve tri kombinacije

rationale.text: His work offers a concrete cross-script retrieval mechanism using phoneme-based token canonicalization, evaluated against relevance-labelled Serbian legal queries.

sources.quote: each token is mapped to a phoneme sequence using deterministic grapheme-to-phoneme rules derived from Serbian orthographic conventions
We evaluated the approach on a manually annotated gold standard of 4 200 query–document relevance pairs drawn from a legal corpus of 38 000 court decisions.

rationale.text: He has investigated query-side transliteration expansion, a relevant candidate for testing alternatives to changes in stored index representations.

sources.quote: This paper studies the effect of automatically expanding queries with their transliteration variants before submission to an inverted index.

rationale.text: His applied work includes search-normalization modules integrated into existing company search systems, although Elasticsearch compatibility remains to be established.

sources.quote: Ovaj rad opisuje iskustva iz tri pilot implementacije interne pretrage zasnovane na open-source pretražnom okviru dopunjenom modulom za normalizaciju pisma
modul integrisan kao dodatak bez izmene ostatka sistema.

rationale.text: He has evaluated deterministic and neural normalization trade-offs under simulated production load, supporting an evidence-based choice rather than assuming a larger model is necessary.

sources.quote: five pipeline configurations ranging from a purely deterministic rule-based normalizer to a full transformer-based normalizer
We measure mean reciprocal rank, P@5, and end-to-end latency at the 50th, 90th, and 99th percentiles on a server cluster of four nodes.

constraints.text: The prototype must address Serbian-specific inflection and mixed scripts, including within-word mixing; whole-sentence transliteration alone does not satisfy the task.

sources.quote: our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.
Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer that was built for Croatian and misses a significant share of Serbian-specific forms.

constraints.text: The approach must work with the existing search setup and support new vocabulary without requiring a full re-index or continued manual synonym-list expansion.

sources.quote: Our current Elasticsearch setup uses a basic stemmer
can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.
maintaining those lists manually does not scale as clients add new product terminology every quarter.

constraints.text: Evaluation must use the company's labelled support data and linguist validation, with an agreed definition of a useful result; the stated acceptance target is below 5% misses with manageable maintenance.

sources.quote: We have a labelled query-response dataset of around 85,000 pairs across all clients, and our two in-house linguists can annotate or validate proposed solutions.
A good outcome is getting that 18% miss rate below 5% and keeping it there with a manageable maintenance process.

constraints.text: Scope must fit approximately EUR 8,000 for tooling or data work and produce something testable within six months; this is not evidence of a funded research contract of that amount.

sources.quote: Budget for tooling or data work is modest — around 8,000 EUR — and we want something testable within six months.

constraints.text: The researcher's contribution must remain a small industrial or consulting engagement with a genuine research component, rather than an unrestricted software-development assignment.

sources.quote: Trenutno je angažovan na dva aktivna projekta, ali ima kapaciteta za jedan manji industrijski ugovor ili konsultantski angažman.
nije zainteresovan za opšte projekte razvoja softvera bez istraživačke komponente.

risks: Transfer is unvalidated: the cited methods were tested mainly on legal, news, web or encyclopedia collections, not LinguaBot's short banking and telecom support queries. The first experiment must separately test morphology, cross-script queries, within-word mixing and unfamiliar product terminology.
The below-5% target may require more than correcting morphology and scripts: the company attributes more than half, but not all, of its current misses to these causes.

Existing evidence does not establish vocabulary updates without full re-indexing in Elasticsearch. Incrementally adding documents is not equivalent to changing normalization rules for already indexed terms.

Foreign names, abbreviations and alphanumeric product strings can defeat deterministic transliteration; neural handling can introduce errors on otherwise regular tokens. Maintenance may remain substantial, as the researcher's company pilots also required terminology updates.
Researcher willingness for a joint project is open, but start date and hours are unknown. His existing commitments and small-engagement capacity may limit delivery within six months.
Data-access permissions, privacy controls, compute resources, latency limits and total collaboration funding are unknown; any could block a realistic deployment or evaluation.
questions: What start date, hours and deliverables can Dragić commit to within his small-engagement capacity, and who among the company's engineers will own integration?
Does the EUR 8,000 cover only tooling and data work, or also researcher fees, infrastructure and deployment? What other funding is available?
Can the researcher access de-identified queries, response documents, relevance labels and index configurations under the necessary client permissions, and are external APIs prohibited for any data?
How is 'no useful result' defined, at what retrieval depth, and can the 12,000-query bank baseline be reproduced? Should acceptance apply separately to each client as well as overall?

Can the first experiment use client- and time-separated held-out data, with linguist-adjudicated slices for inflection, within-word script mixing, exceptions and newly introduced terminology, while checking precision regressions?
Which Elasticsearch version, analyzers and extension mechanisms are available? Does the no-full-re-index requirement apply only to ongoing vocabulary updates, or also to initial installation?
What hardware, peak query load, latency budget and maintenance-effort limit must the prototype meet, and how much annotation time can the two linguists provide?
